title: Unified benchmark workflow — consolidation, trend publication & discoverability
description:
Research pass (2026-08-07) confirms the "unified benchmark workflow" this epic's title refers to is not a green-field build: EPIC-13 through EPIC-21 already constitute it — pytest-benchmark/Locust/LongMemEval foundation (EPIC-13-16), four-tier CI gating (EPIC-17), Db2-specific depth (EPIC-18), the composite Oracle/Mem0/Microsoft-aligned scoring model (EPIC-20, fully Done), and the Microsoft Foundry/AutoGen-shaped agent-quality axis (EPIC-21, fully Done). EPIC-19 ("Reporting, baselines & publication") is the one still-open piece of that arc — BM-26 (rewrite BENCHMARKS.md) and BM-27 (commit baselines.json + regression policy) remain To Do and already fully specify that work; this epic does not duplicate them, it depends on BM-26/BM-27 landing first, same as UNI-3 already declared.

What this epic adds is three gaps the 2026-08-07 audit found that no existing epic covers, verified directly against the repo rather than assumed:

1. **Workflow duplication.** `.github/workflows/benchmarks.yml` (pre-EPIC-17, runs the full pytest-benchmark suite against live Db2 on every push to main, weekly Sunday 04:00 UTC, and manual dispatch) was never reconciled against the four-tier structure EPIC-17 built. `benchmark-scale.yml` (BM-22, EPIC-17's Tier 3) is *also* scheduled Sunday 04:00 UTC, and both publish HTML/JSON to gh-pages independently with no documented relationship between the two report trees. This doubles Db2-container CI cost and leaves it ambiguous which of the two is authoritative.
2. **No trend for the composite score.** UNI-3 built `benchmarks/common/scorecard.py`, which appends a single-run Markdown scorecard section to BENCHMARKS.md each nightly Tier 2 run. Unlike wall-clock metrics (which github-action-benchmark already trend-charts on gh-pages), the composite "Memory Benchmark Score" itself has no historical series anywhere in the repo (`find benchmarks -iname '*history*' -o -iname '*trend*'` returns nothing) — a workflow that recomputes a score nightly but never shows whether it's moving up or down is a series of disconnected snapshots, not a tracked metric.
3. **No single map of the workflow.** Which of the four `.github/workflows/*.yml` files runs when, what tier it belongs to, what it gates (blocking vs. informational), and where its output lands is currently scattered across inline YAML comments, `benchmarks/README.md`, and `BENCHMARK_STRATEGY.md` — there is no one table a new contributor or external auditor can read to understand the whole pipeline in one pass.

WF-1 and WF-3 can start immediately. WF-2 depends on EPIC-19's BM-26 (the document structure it extends) and BM-27 (the baselines a trend is measured against) landing first — same dependency UNI-3 already declared on BM-26/BM-27. This epic is additive-only, same Step 0 philosophy as every prior benchmark epic: no new mandatory infrastructure, no CI gate changes beyond what EPIC-17 already defines.
